item.title: Getting Started with Gatsby in 2025
item.description: A practical guide to setting up a Gatsby blog from scratch — covering setup, markdown, and deployment to GitHub Pages.
item.content:encoded:
Prerequisites

Before you start, make sure you have:

  • Node.js >= 18
  • npm >= 9
  • A GitHub account (for deployment)

Step 1: Install Gatsby CLI

npm install -g gatsby-cli

Verify the install:

gatsby --version

Step 2: Create a new site

gatsby new my-blog
cd my-blog

Step 3: Start the development server

gatsby develop

Visit http://localhost:8000 — your blog is live locally!

You’ll also get GraphiQL at http://localhost:8000/___graphql — a useful tool for exploring your data.

Step 4: Add your first post

Create a file at content/blog/my-first-post/index.md:

---
title: "My First Post"
date: "2025-01-15"
description: "Hello from my Gatsby blog!"
tags: ["meta"]
---

## Hello world

This is my first blog post.

Gatsby hot-reloads, so you’ll see it instantly.

Step 5: Build for production

gatsby build

The output goes to /public. You can preview it with:

gatsby serve

Step 6: Deploy to GitHub Pages

npm install gh-pages --save-dev
npm run deploy

This builds the site and pushes it to the gh-pages branch. Enable GitHub Pages in your repo settings (source: gh-pages branch) and you’re live.

Tips

  • Use gatsby clean when you hit weird caching issues
  • Keep your frontmatter consistent — Gatsby’s GraphQL schema is inferred from your content
  • PrismJS themes are easy to swap — just change the import in Layout.js

Happy blogging!

item.title: Hello World — Why I Started This Blog
item.description: The first post. My motivation for starting a technical blog and what to expect.
item.content:encoded:
Why blog in 2025?

Every developer should write. Not because the world needs another blog — there are plenty — but because writing forces clarity. When you can’t explain something simply, you don’t really understand it.

I’ve been coding for years, taking notes in scattered files, bookmarking articles I never revisit. This blog is me finally organizing those thoughts into something readable and shareable.

What I’ll write about

  • Swift & iOS — native mobile development, SwiftUI, Swift concurrency
  • Kotlin & Android — Jetpack Compose, cross-platform thinking
  • Machine Learning — on-device ML experiments with Core ML and ONNX
  • Minimalism — in code and in life

Who is this for?

Primarily for myself — to solidify my understanding and create a record I can look back on. But if you’re a developer interested in mobile, AI, or clean engineering, hopefully something here is useful to you too.

How often?

No commitments. When I have something worth saying.

Stay tuned.
